rows.selection_reason: No experiments are available yet, so the main uncertainty is the performance floor and whether simple unimodal models are competitive before adding complexity. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA setting, avoiding confounds from image modality, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. It is the best first experiment because it establishes a clean baseline for validation accuracy and F1, enabling later comparisons to isolate the effects of RNA encoders, profile settings, aggregation, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline with modest accuracy (0.485), so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are informative. Testing image-only ResNet-50 with a single profile establishes a simple unimodal baseline for the image modality and reduces uncertainty about a top-level design choice: whether to invest in multimodal fusion at all. This is preferable to immediately testing multiprofile, transformer aggregation, or multimodal fusion because it avoids changing several complex design choices at once and will clarify whether image performance justifies later fusion experiments.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile (accuracy 0.485 vs 0.208, with F1 supporting the same gap), so the next experiment should exploit the RNA direction while testing an important design choice. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and model setting, but changes from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, directly clarifying whether multiple profiles add useful signal before adding more complexity. This is the best use of the next budget slot because it is a minimal, interpretable extension of the current best configuration and helps isolate the effect of profile setting/aggregation.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA multiprofile with PCA2000 and avgpool substantially outperforms single-profile RNA, improving accuracy from 0.485 to 0.591 and F1 from 0.464 to 0.573. The key uncertainty is whether a stronger aggregation method, specifically transformer aggregation, can further improve this promising multiprofile RNA setup. config_003 tests this by changing only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the RNA encoder and profile setting fixed. This is the best next experiment because it directly extends the current best configuration, isolates the effect of aggregation, and avoids confounding changes to modality, encoder, or fusion before it is clear whether more complex aggregation is useful.

Existing evidence shows RNA PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest result so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is weak (0.208 accuracy). It is unclear whether the multiprofile avgpool benefit seen in RNA also applies to the image branch, which is critical before investing in multimodal fusion. config_011 tests this cleanly by keeping ResNet50 and changing only the profile/aggregation setting to multiprofile avgpool relative to config_010. This is the best next experiment because it isolates an important design choice, reduces uncertainty about whether image features can contribute, and avoids prematurely adding fusion or changing multiple factors.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool with PCA is currently the strongest result (0.591 acc, 0.573 F1), and avgpool/multiprofile also outperforms transformer/single in the tested modalities. The key remaining uncertainty in the dominant RNA branch is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA under this best profile/aggregation. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, so it cleanly tests representation. This is the best next step because RNA is the stronger modality, improving it is more likely to yield gains than adding the currently weak image, and it avoids changing fusion/modality simultaneously.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is currently the strongest setting, with scvi_n200 reaching 0.650 accuracy / 0.628 F1 and pca_n2000 reaching 0.591 accuracy / 0.573 F1 under the same profile and aggregation, while image-only models remain much weaker. The main uncertainty is whether the untested scgpt encoder can improve the RNA representation further. config_008 keeps profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool fixed and changes only the RNA encoder to scgpt, directly isolating the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best setting, has high expected immediate performance, and clarifies which RNA encoder should anchor later multimodal or fusion experiments.

RNA-only scvi/multiprofile/avgpool is currently the strongest evidence (0.650 accuracy), while image-only ResNet50 remains weak even with multiprofile avgpool (0.328 accuracy). The key uncertainty is whether a stronger image representation, ViT-L, can make the image modality useful before spending budget on multimodal fusion. config_014 changes only the image encoder relative to config_011 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, so it cleanly isolates image representation. If it substantially improves image accuracy, multimodal ViT-L experiments become justified; if not, the budget should focus on RNA-only or simpler fusion, making this the most efficient next experiment.

The strongest completed model is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), while image-only models are much weaker (best 0.332 accuracy). The major remaining uncertainty is whether image features can usefully complement the best RNA representation. config_036 extends that best RNA setup with the slightly better image encoder (ViT-L avgpool) and a simple concat fusion, keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed to their best-performing values. This directly tests the multimodal design question with a clean baseline fusion choice, helping decide whether further budget should be spent on fusion variants or kept on RNA-only models.

The strongest result is config_036 (0.715 accuracy, 0.687 F1), showing that multimodal scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with multiprofile avgpool and concat is promising, but it is the only multimodal multiprofile result and it is unclear whether multiprofile aggregation is necessary in this setting. config_034 keeps the same RNA encoder, image encoder, and concat fusion but switches to singleprofile/no aggregation, directly testing the profile-setting effect and whether a simpler multimodal model is competitive. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising components while isolating a major design decision, avoids changing multiple factors, and may either yield a strong simpler configuration or justify further investment in multiprofile variants.
